Resurrecting this sub with my stories of ten years in retail!

Many of my customers are temporary workers and their family from India. This leads to some interesting cultural exchange. I've learned everything I know about India from working here.

One of those things is salt. Apparently in parts of India, table salt is commonly sold in large bags stacked outside the store. Imagine their surprise when they ask for salt and I lead them to a tiny cylinder on a shelf next to soup and peanut butter. It got so bad I put up a sign pointing to the shelf.

Then after a few weeks of living stateside, they discover the ins and outs of food labeling. Suddenly they need everything to be gelatin-free (it's not something commonly listed on ingredients lists) and they want to know how to find the expiration date on the salt (there isn't one. It's a preservative.)

I've also had some strange requests. One guy came up to me with a carton of eggs and very genuinely asked me what kind they were. Um, Grade A White? No, are they duck eggs? OH - no, in the US we sell chicken eggs for the most part. I've also been asked at least once a day if we have plain yoghurt. Unfortunately we only carry fruit flavors. It is a drugstore after all.

I've had people genuinely inquire about the proper use of a pregnancy test, suppositories, jock itch cream, and lubricants. Not all at once, fortunately.

Working with immigrants is an enlightening experience and I look forward to each new lesson!
